title: Mean, median, and outlier resistance in regional store performance
scenario_markdown:
A regional retail director reviews the monthly net revenue (in thousands of dollars) across $7$ branch locations in the metropolitan district:

$$\{18,\ 20,\ 22,\ 24,\ 25,\ 26,\ 120\}$$

Six locations are standard suburban strip mall units, while the seventh is an enormous downtown flagship store generating \$120,000 in monthly net revenue. Compute the measures of central location and evaluate which metric best characterizes the performance of a typical branch.
assumptions: Data has a single extreme positive outlier at 120
Sample mean uses n = 7 denominator; median is the 4th ordered value
source_refs: Course Module 1: Descriptive Measures & Basic Probability

approval.notes: Reviewed descriptive statistics calculation: Mean = 255 / 7 = 36.43k, Median = 24.0k. Identifies extreme right skew pulling mean above 6 of the 7 stores, making median the robust representative measure.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the sample mean monthly revenue $\bar{x}$ across all $7$ branch stores?

options.text_markdown: **$\bar{x} = \$24.00$ thousand**: The middle number in the ordered list.
options.hint_markdown: The middle value of an ordered list is the median, not the mean. The mean sums all observations and divides by n.

options.text_markdown: **$\bar{x} = \$42.50$ thousand**: Calculated as $\frac{255}{6}$ using $n - 1$ as the divisor.
options.hint_markdown: Degrees of freedom n - 1 is used when calculating sample variance, never for the sample mean which divides by total count n.

stages.explanation_markdown:
The arithmetic mean sums all observations and divides by the total sample size $n = 7$:

$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x_i}{n} = \frac{18 + 20 + 22 + 24 + 25 + 26 + 120}{7} = \frac{255}{7} \approx 36.4286\text{ (\$36,429)}$$

In Excel: `=AVERAGE(18, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 120)`.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the sample median monthly revenue across the $7$ branches?

options.text_markdown: **$\text{Median} = \$24.00$ thousand ($\\$24{,}000$)**: The 4th observation in the sorted sequence of $7$ values.

options.hint_markdown: The midrange (Min + Max) / 2 is sensitive to extremes; the median is the positional middle value.

options.text_markdown: **$\text{Median} = \$24.50$ thousand**: Average of the 4th and 5th values $\frac{24 + 25}{2}$.
options.hint_markdown: When sample size n is odd (n = 7), the median is uniquely the single central observation at position (n + 1)/2 = 4th.

stages.explanation_markdown:
With $n = 7$ (an odd number), the median is the value at position $(n + 1)/2 = (7 + 1)/2 = 4$ in the sorted array:

$$\{18,\ 20,\ 22,\ \mathbf{24},\ 25,\ 26,\ 120\} \implies \text{Median} = 24.0\text{ (\$24,000)}$$

In Excel: `=MEDIAN(18, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 120)`.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which measure should the regional director rely on to describe the revenue of a **typical** store, and why?

options.text_markdown: **The median ($\\$24{,}000$)**: It is resistant (robust) to extreme outliers; the mean ($\\$36{,}429$) is inflated by the single flagship store so that $6$ of the $7$ branches fall below it.
**The mean ($\\$36{,}429$)**: The mean is always superior because it incorporates every single numerical value in the calculation.
options.hint_markdown: While the mean uses all values, this very property makes it highly sensitive to extreme skew, rendering it unrepresentative of typical observations.

options.text_markdown: **The mode**: Because only repeated values represent true commercial trends.
options.hint_markdown: Here all 7 values are distinct so there is no mode; the median is the standard robust measure of central tendency.

stages.explanation_markdown: The **mean is non-resistant (sensitive to outliers)**: the single extreme observation (\$120k) pulls the mean up to \$36.43k, which is higher than $85.7\%$ ($6$ out of $7$) of the branches. In contrast, the **median is resistant (robust)**: whether the top store made \$30k or \$120k or \$1,000k, the median remains \$24k, accurately reflecting the central revenue of a typical suburban store.
